title: 🕯️ From the Merchant's Desk
subtitle: Notes, letters and half-finished thoughts left upon the desk between journeys.
closingNote: The Merchant writes when the evenings allow.

entries.title: The Traveller with the Emerald Beads
entries.dateLabel: Early August, before the shutters were opened
body: A wandering traveller arrived this morning carrying a small tin box that rattled softly, and would not tell me where it had come from. Inside were emerald beads unlike any I have seen before — green in one light, almost black in another, as though each had swallowed a little of the forest it grew beside.
They are resting on the windowsill now, growing used to the shop. I have not yet decided what they will become. I suspect they already know, and are simply waiting for me to catch up.

entries.title: A Quiet Evening, and Rather a Lot of Candles
entries.dateLabel: A wet evening in late July
body: Rain kept the workshop unusually quiet today. Even the candle flames seemed reluctant to dance.

So I spent the evening sorting the drawer of odd findings — the single clasps, the beads without pairs, the little brass charms whose stories I have long since forgotten. Nothing was finished. Everything was tidied. Some evenings that is exactly the right amount of work.
entries.signoff:
Until our paths cross again,
— The Merchant

entries.title: Autumn at the Workshop Window
entries.dateLabel: The first cool morning of the season
body: Autumn has begun whispering through the workshop windows again. I suspect darker curiosities will soon appear upon the shelves.

There is a particular hour in late summer when the light turns the colour of old honey and everything upon the workbench looks faintly enchanted. I have been gathering amber, smoke-grey glass and a small handful of acorn caps found along the lane. Something is coming. I am not entirely certain what yet.
